title: Static and Machine
premise: Casper Eriksen has built her life on being forgettable: a cargo hauler, an insurance investigator of impossible accidents, a woman with no flag and no history. But when she decodes a distress signal written in a language extinct for two centuries—the language of her own erased homeworld—she learns the 'accidents' she's been investigating were cover-ups for a corporate program harvesting the survivors' descendants. Racing a rival salvage fleet to a relay at the edge of dead space, Casper gathers a ragtag found family aboard her ship, the Vellum, and discovers the signal is a countdown: a dead-man's archive that will expose the program but also paint a target on everyone she loves. In the end, Casper chooses to broadcast the archive at the cost of the Vellum and her own anonymity, trading invisibility for a name—and a family—that no one can take back.
about_author: C. M. Winterbourne is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to frequencies no one else answered. They write about people who survive by staying quiet, and what happens when silence finally fails them.

chapters.title: The Quiet Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Investigating a cargo ship's 'impossible' decompression in contested orbit, Casper notices the accident report has been edited by someone with corporate clearance. Emotional beat: the comfort of routine curdling into unease as she realizes her invisibility has limits.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Alone on the Vellum, she intercepts a repeating transmission in Old Vessic—a language extinct since the Purging, and the tongue of her erased childhood. Emotional beat: vertigo and grief; a ghost language calling her by a name she buried.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Cross-referencing the signal's coordinates with fifteen years of 'impossible accident' files, she finds a pattern: every wreck carried Vessic descendants. Emotional beat: cold fury as coincidence becomes conspiracy.

chapters.title: Passengers at Meridian Dock
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Fleeing an audit notice, she takes on three undocumented passengers: ex-fleet medic Idris, teenage stowaway Juno, and a silent old woman who speaks Vessic. Emotional beat: wary hospitality—the first crack in her isolation.

chapters.title: The Old Woman's Grammar
chapters.summary: POV Idris. The passenger, Sefa, begins translating the signal: it's a dead-man's archive, set to broadcast evidence of the Harvest Program unless someone reaches the relay to renew—or silence—it. Emotional beat: Idris's guilt over fleet service meeting Casper's dawning purpose.

chapters.title: Impossible Accident, Repeated
chapters.summary: POV Casper. A corporate 'investigator' boards them at a fuel depot, asking precisely the wrong questions. Casper recognizes her own old methods turned predatory. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing she has become the hunted.

chapters.title: Juno's Frequency
chapters.summary: POV Juno. The stowaway, a self-taught radio prodigy, cracks the signal's handshake protocol and accidentally pings their position to the rival salvage fleet, the Kestrel Combine. Emotional beat: shame, and Casper choosing mentorship over rage—found family forming under pressure.

chapters.title: Burn Toward Dead Space
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The Vellum runs dark through a debris field to evade Combine interceptors, Idris patching a failing reactor by hand. Emotional beat: terror transformed into trust; the crew becomes a crew.

chapters.title: What the Fleet Did to Vess
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. In fragments, Sefa recounts the Purging: the colony sold for parts, the survivors indentured, the language banned. Emotional beat: mourning made communal; Casper hears her own half-remembered childhood confirmed.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: POV Casper. They reach dead space's threshold and find the relay not abandoned but inhabited—a hermit archivist, Oyelaran, who has guarded the archive for forty years and distrusts everyone. Emotional beat: hope meeting paranoia at the door.

chapters.title: Terms of Custody
chapters.summary: POV Oyelaran. Oyelaran tests the newcomers, forcing Casper to prove her lineage and her intent. Emotional beat: an interrogation that becomes an inheritance; the archive's custodian passing the weight on.

chapters.title: The Countdown in the Static
chapters.summary: POV Juno. Decoding the archive's timer, Juno discovers it broadcasts in eleven days whether they act or not—exposing the Program, and painting every Vessic descendant as a target. Emotional beat: the double edge of truth; victory and doom in the same waveform.

chapters.title: Kestrel at the Door
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The Combine fleet arrives, offering amnesty for the archive—and revealing that Casper's own edited accident reports were her employer's contribution to the cover-up. Emotional beat: betrayal; her old life weaponized against her.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Looking Away
chapters.summary: POV Casper. In a quiet night watch, Casper confesses to Idris how many reports she signed that kept the Program invisible. Emotional beat: reckoning with complicity; love offered despite it.

chapters.title: The Combine's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Idris. Captured briefly during a boarding action, Idris learns the Combine plans to suppress the archive and harvest the relay's fusion core, killing the station. He escapes to warn them. Emotional beat: duty inverted—he betrays his old uniform to keep his new family.

chapters.title: Sabotage in the Dark
chapters.summary: POV Juno. The crew sabotages the Combine's boarding tender in the relay's crawlspaces; Sefa is gravely injured shielding Juno. Emotional beat: the cost of resistance made flesh; fear sharpening resolve.

chapters.title: Sefa's Last Transmission
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Dying, Sefa records a final message in Vessic to be included in the broadcast—a living voice for a dead language. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into legacy; the language breathes again.

chapters.title: The Choice of Names
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The archive can broadcast wide—hitting every Vessic descendant with exposure—or narrow, sparing them but letting the Program continue. The crew votes; Casper must break the tie. Emotional beat: the weight of power, and the corruption it whispers.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Climax. Under Combine fire, they seize the relay's transmitter and send the full archive—every crime, every name—while the Vellum's reactor burn masks their signal. Emotional beat: defiant, costly triumph; the truth screaming across dead space.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: POV Idris. The Combine fractures as its crimes go public; colonies rise; warrants fly. The Vellum is crippled, Sefa gone, the relay dying around them. Emotional beat: exhaustion and raw, uncertain hope.

chapters.title: A Name No One Can Revoke
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Rescued by Vessic descendant ships answering the broadcast, Casper gives her real name for the first time in fifteen years. Emotional beat: vulnerability as arrival; invisibility surrendered willingly.

chapters.title: Static and Machine
chapters.summary: POV Juno. Months later, the patched Vellum runs cargo again—no longer hiding, crewed by family. Juno, now the ship's signal-keeper, teaches Vessic to new passengers. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace; the signal answered at last.
